applicabilityConditions.absenceDefinition: a species was treated as lacking a DFA if it had no DFA hit and also had more than 6,000 proteins in UniProt the criteria are liberal and likely produce false negatives, especially for species with far more than 6,000 proteins, so DFA prevalence across the fungal tree is probably underestimated
applicabilityConditions.note: conclusions are bounded by which traits had usable public data, not by which traits are biologically plausible
applicabilityConditions.phylogeny: TimeTree database web interface; the resulting tree represented 85 fungal orders
applicabilityConditions.proteinFamily: structurally divergent fungal actins, defined as ProteinCartography clusters LC04, LC11 and LC14
applicabilityConditions.statistics: model selection comparing a model in which DFA presence/absence and the trait share an evolutionary trajectory against a model in which they evolved independently, scored by Akaike information criterion where the lowest AIC wins phylogeny-corrected generalized linear mixed model (logistic regression) testing whether variation in the continuous trait accounts for variation in DFA status while controlling for shared evolutionary history; a slope significantly different from zero would indicate a correlation
applicabilityConditions.traitSource: Fun Fun: aggregates species-level ecological, cellular and biochemical trait information from multiple studies, including FUNGuild classifications of ecological function and trophic mode
applicabilityConditions.unitOfObservation: species, not independent observations; phylogenetic non-independence is modelled explicitly

confidence.basis: no positive control on the trait-mapping method, an average of 34 species per trait, six traits chosen for data availability rather than biological relevance, and an absence criterion the authors expect to produce false negatives

cost.note: computational study; 853 species in the working set, 102 analysed; no monetary or compute cost is reported

ATP-binding residues are conserved; residues required for polymerization are not well conserved.

hypothesis: Test whether phylogenetic trait mapping can reveal the function of a structurally divergent actin isoform found across fungi, by asking whether any of six species-level fungal traits predicts the presence or absence of that isoform.
invalidators: a trait panel with better coverage in which an association is recovered
a positive control showing the method recovers a known protein-trait association at comparable sample sizes
a knockout of the divergent actin in a tractable species producing a characterised phenotype
nextSteps: Expand the range of traits tested for correlation with DFA presence, which would require more complete datasets covering multiple species whose DFA status can be established; fungal ecology groups and mycologists may have the tools and knowledge to generate such information.

Focus on genetic traits using public genomic information: search for correlation between DFA presence or absence and the presence or absence of gene families across genomes of species with confident DFA status.
Probe DFA function directly by knocking out the DFA in a genetically tractable species and characterising the resulting phenotypes.
openQuestions: What function do divergent fungal actins perform, given conserved ATP-binding residues but poorly conserved polymerization residues?
Would a trait panel chosen for biological relevance rather than data availability recover an association?
outcomeSummary: The divergent actin was mapped across 853 fungal species and found to be evolutionarily labile, unlike canonical actin. None of six curated traits predicted its presence, so its function remains unknown and the project was iced for lack of usable trait data.
provenanceNotes: Icebox statement: We've decided to put this project on ice. We think there may be interesting biology underlying divergent fungal actins, but the approach we took here to elucidate it was limited by the availability of relevant trait information. The pub carries no Icebox hashtag; the reason is stated in prose as limited availability of relevant trait information, which is recorded as a resource constraint.

Absence is inferred, not observed: a species was treated as lacking a DFA if it had no DFA hit and also had more than 6,000 proteins in UniProt the criteria are liberal and likely produce false negatives, especially for species with far more than 6,000 proteins, so DFA prevalence across the fungal tree is probably underestimated
Trait categories were recoded after inspecting the data to keep at least four species per level, which is recorded as a protocol adaptation rather than as a pre-specified design.

no multiple-comparison correction is reported across the six traits; the discrete tests are AIC model selection rather than null-hypothesis tests, and the two continuous tests report uncorrected p-values
Part of the Arcadia platform effort 'Annotation: Mapping the functional landscape of protein families across biology'.
question: Can phylogenetic trait mapping reveal the function of a structurally divergent actin isoform conserved across fungi, by finding a species-level trait that predicts its presence or absence?

successCriteria: At least one fungal trait whose evolutionary history is better explained by a model correlated with divergent actin presence than by an independent model, or a continuous trait whose slope on divergent actin presence differs significantly from zero.
